I'm assuming there's no physical medical reason for this.

If he shits his pants, make him clean the underwear in a bucket. Logical and immediate consequence. If he shits in the toilet, give him a small reward. After he doesn't shit his pants for a predetermined period of time (maybe 2 weeks - long enough so you know he is capable of shitting in the toilet every time, but not so long that he gets dissuaded) he can have a special outing to get underwear, or if that's not an option then he could choose some from a catalogue or website you show him.

As many people have mentioned, this behavior is usually a sign of a deeper problem. Usually psychological. Please do not punish or scold him in anyway for this behavior. There are many reasons why he maybe doing this...

  1. He was never properly potty trained.

  2. Sometimes kids that have unstable homes (like those from divorce, foster systems, etc) will develop an emotional attachment to their poop. Being something physical, something that they can depend on, and something that they know is theirs (because it comes from them) it's something they'll want to keep because there's a sense of control in that.

  3. Potty Training regression due to added stress (such as a new sibling.) "The baby wears diapers and gets lots of attention. I want to wear diapers too. If I poop my pants, they'll put me into diapers, and then I'll get lots of attention."

You should definitely seek out professional psychological help to help diagnose any underlying issues he maybe dealing with. At least someone for the kid to talk to. While working with him on the potty training, try to be as patient as possible. If you get too frustrated, step out of the room. Always ask him to do as much of the cleaning as possible. At the age of 7 he should be able to handle cleaning himself up, and doing his own laundry. Explain what happens when you lay in your own excrement (sores, infections, etc) and emphasize how serious the injuries can be.

I'm sure you wouldn't be able to do this without getting into some sort of serious trouble, but let him run around without underwear or pants on inside the house. (Have him wear a robe or something) This has helped me potty train my son. Without anything to wear, he doesn't have anything to poop into, and he is always more anxious to use the toilet so he doesn't potty on himself or make a mess anywhere else. He's also more confident because he doesn't have to fiddle with the buttons or pulling down his pants. He may just be having issues pulling down his pants, but is too uncomfortable/nervous to say anything about it.

Whatever the case, just offer loads of love and understanding. You're an amazing person for offering your home to others, especially children without anywhere else to go. I've always wanted to adopt or be a foster parent but it's not for everyone, and unfortunately, my SO is one of those people.

If this is the case, then I think the question another commenter posed regarding "which rights?" is key. In the United States, we tout the rights of "Life, Liberty, and the pursuit of Happiness." Well... all of these rights are founded on the implicit understanding that humans are mortal, and it takes us a relatively long time to accomplish things. We accept the notion that people have a right to life (save the Capital Punishment arguments for another thread), but what if we didn't die of old age or disease? Happiness? Say the AI really liked investing. Is an AI really allowed to invest $1000 and let it compound over the next thousand years until the interest dwarfs the sum of all human economies? Is it a human right to reproduce? I imagine most people think so, but this notion is predicated on an understanding that people just can't make that many babies, and every human birth is to some degree offset by a human death. Neither would be true with AI replication. Depending on the storage needs of the AI, it could theoretically be the most populous "race" in the world literally overnight.
